(i) the sound wave properties in disordered solids are profoundly affected by the presence of elastic heterogeneities; (ii) the extent and nature of these heterogeneities can be quantified by means of an order parameter, the so-called elastic heterogeneity index, which is defined as the ratio of the standard deviations of the elastic moduli and the average values; and (iii) the sound wave features are correlated with this order parameter, which is a macroscopic thermodynamically relevant quantity

(i) the sound wave properties are strongly affected by the elastic heterogeneity at nanoscale; (ii) this effect is particularly pronounced in the glassy phase; (iii) the elastic heterogeneity is the result of the interplay between the disorder and the mechanical response of the material, which is strongly anharmonic in the glassy state.
